items.headline: Man, 25, charged with murder of 29-year-old found dead on a Tuas South road
items.summary: Police were called to Tuas South on Aug 29 and found a 29-year-old man motionless on the road; he was pronounced dead at the scene. A 25-year-old man was charged the next day with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code.

items.headline: Tan See Leng says Singapore's next growth phase must create more value, not use more land
items.summary: Manpower and Trade Minister Tan See Leng said Singapore can no longer grow by adding land, workers or carbon emissions, and must instead raise the value it draws from what it already has as it plans its next economic phase.

items.headline: Arrest warrant issued for Lim Tean after he fails to surrender to begin jail term
items.summary: A warrant of arrest was issued for lawyer and former opposition politician Lim Tean after he did not surrender himself to court to start serving a jail term.

items.headline: Singaporean once reported missing in Vietnam arrested over alleged vape syndicate link
items.summary: A Singaporean who had earlier been reported missing in Vietnam was arrested over an alleged link to a syndicate supplying etomidate-laced vape liquid, part of a widening crackdown on the drug-laced pods.

items.headline: India rushes rescue teams to Nepal as flood toll climbs and citizens stay unreachable
items.summary: India stepped up its response to the Himalayan floods, sending medical and tunnel-rescue specialists to help reach trapped hydropower workers, after New Delhi said scores of its citizens remained unreachable in the disaster zone.

items.headline: NSE targets a record $55 billion valuation in its September IPO
items.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India, the world's largest derivatives exchange by volume, is seeking a valuation of as much as 5.26 trillion rupees (about $55 billion) in an initial public offering expected in the second half of September.

items.headline: RBI projects about $80 billion in inflows from measures to steady the rupee
items.summary: Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the central bank expects to draw at least $80 billion in foreign-currency inflows from recent steps to attract dollars, as it defends the rupee against pressure from higher oil prices.

items.headline: Nepal set to turn to India for power after floods knock out hydro output
items.summary: Nepal is likely to lean on electricity imports from India after the Himalayan floods damaged hydropower plants that supply much of its grid, according to people familiar with the matter.

items.headline: Chancellor Healey vows a 'drama-free' Oct 28 budget within the fiscal rules
items.summary: Chancellor John Healey called fiscal discipline the 'bedrock' of the Labour government and pledged a low-drama first budget on Oct 28, insisting he and Prime Minister Andy Burnham will stay within their fiscal rules despite mounting spending pressures.

items.headline: Burnham's government leaves the door open to a higher bank tax
items.summary: The UK government declined to rule out raising taxes on banks in Burnham's first budget, as bumper profits at lenders fuel speculation the administration will target City of London firms to help fund its pledges.

items.headline: Burnham vows a 'huge transfer of power' from the Treasury to the north
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged a 'huge transfer of power' away from the Treasury toward the regions, a devolution push he casts as central to his growth agenda.

items.headline: Update: Nepal-Tibet flood toll climbs past 760 with more than 900 workers missing
items.summary: The death toll from the Himalayan glacier-collapse floods rose to at least 762 in Nepal, plus 16 in China, with more than 900 workers still missing at hydropower sites. About 90 Americans are among the unaccounted-for as rescuers regain ground access to Rasuwa.

items.headline: Russian strike on a munitions depot near Kyiv kills 38, the year's deadliest attack
items.summary: President Zelensky said the death toll from a Russian drone strike on an arms depot in the village of Myla, near Kyiv, rose to 38 — the deadliest attack of the year — with secondary explosions damaging dozens of buildings, including a care home.

items.headline: Gaza ceasefire teeters as Israel escalates strikes after Kushner talks stall
items.summary: Israel resumed strikes on Gaza within hours of US envoy Jared Kushner leaving talks with Prime Minister Netanyahu, as the two sides stay deadlocked over sequencing Hamas's disarmament against an Israeli withdrawal.

items.headline: Ukraine sets a Russian refinery ablaze in Krasnodar in its deep-strike campaign
items.summary: Ukrainian drones struck an oil refinery in Russia's Krasnodar region, killing two and starting a fire, part of Kyiv's sustained campaign against Russian energy infrastructure even as Moscow threatens mass strikes on Ukraine's own power grid.

items.headline: OpenAI says its new 'Jalapeno' chips beat Nvidia's in internal tests
items.summary: OpenAI said its in-house 'Jalapeno' AI processors outperformed Nvidia's current chips in testing, leading on performance per watt and on response speed, underscoring its push to cut reliance on Nvidia hardware.

items.headline: Apple unveils new Mac mini and Mac Studio with major chip upgrades
items.summary: Apple announced refreshed Mac mini and Mac Studio desktops with significant processor upgrades, aimed at developers and AI workloads.

items.headline: XPeng's robotics unit to raise $900 million from Alibaba and Tencent
items.summary: XPeng's robotics arm plans to raise about $900 million from backers including Alibaba and Tencent, valuing the unit at more than $6 billion as the Chinese automaker races to mass-produce its IRON humanoid robot.

items.headline: Broadcom seeks more than $60 billion in debt to finance AI chips
items.summary: Broadcom is in talks with lenders to raise more than $60 billion in debt for an AI chip financing arrangement that would benefit customers including Anthropic, one of the largest such packages yet in the AI buildout.

items.headline: Meta agrees to a $16.7 billion settlement with US states over child safety
items.summary: Meta and a coalition of state attorneys general settled a federal case alleging it misrepresented the mental-health harms of Facebook and Instagram to children; Meta will pay up to $16.7 billion and add new safeguards for under-18 users.

items.headline: Corn and wheat futures jump to their highest in more than three years
items.summary: Wheat settled 3.1% higher at 784 cents a bushel and corn rose to 536.5 cents on Friday, both at multi-year highs as war and heat across the Ukraine-Russia breadbasket squeeze global grain supply.

items.headline: Quantum-computing firm Pasqal surges in its New York debut via a SPAC merger
items.summary: France-based Pasqal began trading in New York after merging with Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp II, its shares jumping on debut and outpacing other recently listed quantum-computing companies.

items.headline: China's industrial profits climb 17.6% as Asia-Pacific markets end mixed
items.summary: Chinese industrial profits rose 17.6% from a year earlier, though the pace cooled from the first half, as Asia-Pacific markets closed mixed on Friday with investors weighing the Fed's Jackson Hole signals.

items.headline: 🏎️ Norris wins a chaotic Dutch Grand Prix as Verstappen crashes out on lap 1
items.summary: Lando Norris took back-to-back wins at Zandvoort, leading home Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, while home favourite Max Verstappen crashed out on the opening lap in slippery conditions to bring out the red flags.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli takes a 59-point title lead into Monza
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli's runner-up finish stretched his championship lead to 59 points over George Russell, with Norris now 83 points back, as Formula 1 heads to Monza for the Italian Grand Prix on Sept 4-6.

items.headline: 🏏 India rout Thailand by 94 runs to open their Women's Asia Cup campaign
items.summary: India posted 159 for 9 and bowled Thailand out for 65 in Dubai; Shafali Verma top-scored with 64 and Deepti Sharma, in her 150th T20I, took three wickets in seven balls without conceding a run.

items.headline: 🎾 Alcaraz opens his US Open title defence, his first match since an April wrist injury
items.summary: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz begins his US Open campaign against Roman Safiullin as the main draw gets under way, playing his first singles match since a right-wrist injury in April, with Jannik Sinner absent injured.

items.headline: Astronomers find a star, S301, whipping around the Milky Way's black hole
items.summary: Researchers identified S301, a star on a tight, fast orbit around Sagittarius A*, offering a new way to measure the spin of the Milky Way's central supermassive black hole through relativistic effects on its orbit.

items.headline: A four-carbon sugar is detected in an interstellar cloud
items.summary: Astronomers detected erythrulose, a four-carbon sugar, in a molecular cloud near the galactic centre using the Yebes and IRAM radio telescopes, the kind of prebiotic molecule that could seed the chemistry of life.

items.headline: Deep imaging reveals a swarm of bow-shock waves in the outer Helix Nebula
items.summary: New deep images of the Helix Nebula uncovered numerous curved bow shocks in its outer regions, formed as shells of gas thrown off by the dying Sun-like star break up and race outward.

items.headline: A Cretaceous 'Age of Dinosaurs' seafloor is identified deep beneath the Pacific
items.summary: Scientists reported evidence of ancient seafloor dating to the age of dinosaurs preserved deep beneath the modern Pacific Ocean, a rare window into the planet's Mesozoic oceans.

fun_fact.headline: Flamingos are born grey and turn pink from their diet
fun_fact.body: Flamingos are not born pink. Chicks hatch a dull grey or white and only turn pink because their diet of algae and brine shrimp is loaded with carotenoid pigments - the same family of compounds (beta-carotene) that colours carrots. A flamingo kept off those foods slowly fades back to pale, so a bird's brightness is essentially a readout of how well it has been eating.

puzzle.title: The Night Watchman
puzzle.body:
A museum night watchman went to his supervisor and said he had had a vivid dream that thieves would break in and steal a priceless painting that very night. He urged that extra guards be posted.

The supervisor thanked him warmly. The next morning nothing had been stolen - yet the watchman was fired anyway. Why?
puzzle.approach: Take the watchman's story literally and ask what it reveals about him, not about the theft.
puzzle.answer: He was paid to stay awake all night guarding the museum. By reporting a dream he had had ‘that night,’ he admitted he had fallen asleep on duty. Whether or not the dream came true was beside the point: confessing to dreaming on shift was confessing to sleeping on the job.

word_puzzle.title: Back to School
word_puzzle.body:
Rearrange all 12 letters of the phrase

THE CLASSROOM

to reveal the person once in charge of it. (One word, 12 letters.)
word_puzzle.approach: Every letter of the clue phrase is reused exactly once to build the answer.
word_puzzle.answer:
SCHOOLMASTER.

It is an exact anagram of THE CLASSROOM — both use the letters A, C, E, H, L, M, O, O, R, S, S, T.
